description: For each past occurrence of the event, the move of the market (market: US = the S&P 500 via SPY, the default for US events; HK = the Hang Seng Index, from its first close after the news; 'measured' in the answer names it) 2 weeks, 4 weeks and 3 months later (fractions: 0.037 = +3.7%), plus median, share up, worst and best beside any window of the same length. With too few occurrences only the list is given. Give symbol (a ticker or company name of the measured market) to measure that one stock's own price, dividends included, instead of the market (QQQ for the Nasdaq-100). Use for questions like 'what happens to stocks after a midterm election / an FOMC meeting', 'what did AAPL do after CPI' or 'what did Hong Kong do after the Fed'.
name: event_study
title: What the market did after an event
